location.evidence: Most of the lowest-paying programs are in Puerto Rico. Federal wage data show workers in the San Juan area earn far less than mainland workers, and every major occupational group there pays below its national average.

prestige.evidence: The best-paying programs are at schools that admit few applicants. Colleges like Colgate report graduates going to employers and top graduate schools through organized career pipelines that have little to do with the psychology major itself.

stepping_stone.evidence: A Georgetown analysis reported by the American Psychological Association found psychology majors earn graduate degrees at a higher rate than college graduates overall, often in counseling, social work, education or other fields.

programs.evidence: Stanford admits very few applicants, and its psychology department says the major prepares students for careers in business, law and medicine, so its graduates reach well-paid employers.
Santa Clara is not highly selective but sits in Silicon Valley, and its admissions materials point to internships and jobs at nearby tech employers such as Apple, Google and Meta.
Colgate is a highly selective liberal arts college, and it tracks graduates going on to employers and top graduate schools through a structured career program.
